title: Labyrinth
build: Two-sided English disk edition; stored credit at $743D-$747D includes V 1.0 V; supplied G64 preservation images

records.c: Persistent nickel-disposition byte. Taking the dropped nickel at $92CE stores one; the first accepted return at $944B stores $FF. During an accepted popcorn offer in main theater nine, $9485 compares exactly with one: equal removes the whole box through $087F and prints $80A7; other values print $80F6 and retain the box. The counter return is live checked; both later offer branches are isolated original-code tests with nonnegative conversation state.

Forty-two consecutive three-byte JMP stubs expose resident services to loaded overlays, followed by RTS at $087E. Targets include map classification, message display, inventory mutation, clock penalties, audio, random state, slot dialogs and descriptor setup. The stubs are executable calls, not a table of interleaved pointer words; each destination is traced separately for the opening's resident image.

Y is loaded from selected inventory slot $666F. Reject zero and the end index $667B through $09DF; a negative inventory byte returns without removal. Otherwise subtract one from $6729,Y, then redraw the inventory and adjust its selection through $08A8. Counts use zero for one unit and a negative byte for absence. The ticket purchase uses this routine after subtracting four from the dollar entry, charging the fifth dollar here.

1-byte resident field at $08D3, holding 00 in the captured opening. Direct code references: $08D4 sta $08D3; $08DD lda $08D3. These are the direct instruction accesses in the decoded image; indexed access bounds and indirect callers require their enclosing routine. The listed bytes describe the captured value.

Preserve the replacement block value at $08D3, classify the current map cell, replace its pickup representation through $09A5, and derive the inventory slot from the complemented block-class result. Extend the inventory bound if necessary, mark its description request, and increment the stored count with negative values treated as absent. Counts below nine are stored; larger counts select the capacity message. On success select the item, present its description, redraw inventory and mark the wheel state. This entry follows the runtime replacement byte at $08D3.

1-byte resident field at $0927, holding 00 in the captured opening. Direct code references: $0916 sta $0927; $0936 sty $0927; $0952 lda $0927; $0A58 ldy $0927. These are the direct instruction accesses in the decoded image; indexed access bounds and indirect callers require their enclosing routine. The listed bytes describe the captured value.

For a negative request A, clear its high bit and set the later sprite-restore flag to zero; a nonnegative request sets that flag negative. Store the description request at $6994 and enter $0939 to present it.

Disable sprites, open the selected message window, wait for joystick fire to be released, and unless finished-game state equals one run the bounded input/delay helper with X=eight. Restore sprites if $0927 permits and clear elapsed movement counter $DC before returning.

Select request index $BD or $3D from A's sign. Patch the split description pointer at $6C7B/$6C3E from Y/X and enter the ordinary request-description path at $0928. This is a pointer override for one message slot.
Set Y=two, call the shared block/limit classifier beginning $4173, and enter $099B to return the current map cell's low nibble in A and its classification in X.

Call $4171 to update the player's map-column and block-limit fields, then use $AF to fetch the map cell low nibble and return block type $B0 in X. The secondary-object entry shares the final map read at $099B.

Record the map mutation through $58C8. Scenes eleven and twenty-three mirror the same change into each other's saved mutation records by temporarily substituting the scene index and calling $58DE. Restore the original scene, clear pending request $0530 to zero, and return. Other scenes still clear that request after the single mutation.
Store X in scene-entry field $0532 and Y in pending scene $0530, then return. This seven-byte helper changes the request without loading it immediately.
Load A with five and fall through into $09DF, which installs the text pointer from Y/X and uses A as the text indent value at $0342.

For up to X groups of sixty decrements of $030E, watch keyboard-queue growth and joystick state $030C. A new keyboard byte is removed when it aborts the wait. Before returning, wait for joystick fire to be released, set the fire latch, and clear the wheel-prefix length.

For each count in Y, set IRQ-maintained downcounter $030E to sixty and call $0A6D until it becomes zero, then decrement Y. Returns when the requested number of sixty-tick intervals has completed. The tick-to-wall-time rate depends on the running raster standard.
Store A into $030E and busy-wait until the IRQ service decrements it to zero. Unlike $0A27, this helper does not poll for an early input abort.

1-byte resident field at $0A76, holding 00 in the captured opening. Direct code references: $0A03 sta $0A76; $0A23 lda $0A76; $0A77 sta $0A76; $0A8B cmp $0A76; $0A92 lda $0A76. These are the direct instruction accesses in the decoded image; indexed access bounds and indirect callers require their enclosing routine. The listed bytes describe the captured value.

Cache threshold A. Negative room-text mode first checks its signed threshold/proximity gate, then compares $0971's distance result with the threshold. On success return to the caller. On failure discard the caller return address from the stack and display either the no-person or nobody-nearby message with indent five. The threshold value $25 selects the former reply. This is a control-flow guard used by interaction scripts.
Return the stored count/availability byte $6729,Y in A without converting the zero-based quantity or negative absent marker.

Patch the zero-terminated blocked-entry list pointer at $0AE5 from X/Y. Reset word-wheel mode and colours, clear the relevant available verb/object fields, explicitly disable several fixed entries, and enable the hint verb selected by persistent $056F. For each byte in the supplied list, mark that global availability entry negative. On zero terminator, select the default verb/destination and adjust the final-scene controls through $0B21 where needed, switch/redraw wheels, and reset the active wheel to zero. The descriptor/availability arrays are runtime copies, not scene code.
Byte 1 of the instruction at $0AE5 (lda $1000,y). This is a patched operand/instruction alias, not a separately callable routine. Execution continues on the enclosing instruction boundaries.
Byte 2 of the instruction at $0AE5 (lda $1000,y). This is a patched operand/instruction alias, not a separately callable routine. Execution continues on the enclosing instruction boundaries.

High operand byte of JSR $5E1D at $0AFE. The continuation switches the wheel again, clears the selected wheel display through $6000, sets active wheel zero, and returns. It is part of the inventory/action setup preceding this address, not a separate inventory data list.
Four dictionary indices for the final-scene verb choices, copied by $0B21 into the runtime wheel selector table. The following four destination indices at $0B1D are a separate table.
Four dictionary indices copied with the final-scene verbs into the destination selector table. The final-scene setup enables all four paired choices and changes the two wheel bounds to four.

Copy the four verb and object dictionary indices from $0B19/$0B1D into runtime selectors, clear their availability/object-kind fields, select slot two in both wheels, and set their upper bounds to four. The actual final-scene response code is in its later overlay, outside the opening analysis.
Increment persistent byte $0568 unless it already equals $7F. This is the positive saturation entry; the opposite helper at $0B59 stops at $80.
Decrement $0568 unless it equals $80, preserving the negative signed-byte saturation endpoint. Other additions through $9676 wrap rather than using this saturation helper.
JMP $6923, exposing the upper-message clear routine through the resident overlay API. The following bytes hold message/work templates, not additional clear instructions.

Headered clock message: first bytes $00/$F7, then "You have XX hours, XX minutes left." and zero. $0B8E patches the two decimal fields and plural suffixes before $09DF displays it; the stored placeholder bytes are mutable output within this bounded template.

Offset 1 in clock_message_template ($0B67-$0B8D). Headered clock message: first bytes $00/$F7, then "You have XX hours, XX minutes left." and zero. $0B8E patches the two decimal fields and plural suffixes before $09DF displays it; the stored placeholder bytes are mutable output within this bounded template.

Headered clock message: first bytes $00/$F7, then "You have XX hours, XX minutes left." and zero. $0B8E patches the two decimal fields and plural suffixes before $09DF displays it; the stored placeholder bytes are mutable output within this bounded template.

Offset 31 in clock_message_template ($0B67-$0B8D). Headered clock message: first bytes $00/$F7, then "You have XX hours, XX minutes left." and zero. $0B8E patches the two decimal fields and plural suffixes before $09DF displays it; the stored placeholder bytes are mutable output within this bounded template.

Patch the hour/minute template with decimal values from $0376/$0375. A value of one blanks the plural s using glyph $40; otherwise restore s. $0BFD writes the two visible decimal digits, suppressing a leading zero. Show the headered message at $0B67 with indent two. The countdown decrement itself is $0BC7.

Outside scene $1A, decrement the frame subcounter $0373. On underflow reload $3B and borrow through seconds $0374, minutes $0375, and hours $0376; seconds and minutes reload to $3B. If hours underflow, clear $0580. The real-time rate depends on the IRQ path that calls this routine and is measured separately.

Reduce input A modulo one hundred, divide that remainder into tens and units by repeated subtraction of ten, and write the unit ASCII digit at $0B68,Y. Write the tens digit at $0B67,Y, replacing a leading zero with $40 so the stream parser suppresses it. This formatter does not display a hundreds digit.

Selected item codes seventeen and fourteen queue sounds $2D and $10. Item zero presents the peach/sleep response and, depending on room text mode, either restores a saved return scene or uses $0C61's one-hour penalty. Clear the related player action $03A6 afterward. Other item codes return without these effects.

Load message request $39 and enter $0C63, which displays it, decrements hour field $0376, and clears finished-game state $0580 if the hour becomes negative. A caller can enter $0C63 with a different message request.

Send sound request A through $0928, decrement remaining hour/penalty byte $0376, and clear running flag $0580 when the result becomes negative. $0C61 selects sound $39 before entering this shared body.

In a nonnegative room-text mode, print the special headered message at $0EBA. Otherwise display message $35, subtract ten minutes from $0375, and on borrow add sixty and decrement the hour. This path changes the clock fields directly rather than waiting for real-time ticks.

Extend inventory end index $667B if selected slot X reaches it, add A to that slot's stored count, clamp results at eight, select the slot, redraw inventory, and mark the companion wheel state. Stored count eight represents nine owned units, so this helper enforces the one-digit display bound.

Inspect persistent mode $057A, advance its zero/negative paths and choose one of three headered replies. Set player colour $0244 to eleven or the chosen favourite colour, request a sprite swap through $63, and display the selected reply with indent five. These are the explicit state transitions; the caller determines which object interaction triggers them.
Three cached arguments for $0CE8: input Y, input A and sound request X. The helper uses them to compute a note and patch an effect template.

1-byte resident field at $0CE6, holding 00 in the captured opening. Direct code references: $0CEB sta $0CE6; $0CF5 sbc $0CE6. These are the direct instruction accesses in the decoded image; indexed access bounds and indirect callers require their enclosing routine. The listed bytes describe the captured value.

1-byte resident field at $0CE7, holding 00 in the captured opening. Direct code references: $0CEE stx $0CE7; $0CFF ldy $0CE7; $0D21 lda $0CE7. These are the direct instruction accesses in the decoded image; indexed access bounds and indirect callers require their enclosing routine. The listed bytes describe the captured value.

Cache Y/A/X, compute seven times A plus Y modulo 256 into $0D27, choose the default effect-template pointer for request X from $1F33/$1F6E, and bank I/O out. Convert note index $63 minus the computed byte through $25FA, restore I/O, and queue the original request through $1C0C. The frequency bytes in the template are runtime modifications of the effect data.
Runtime byte seven*A+Y produced by $0CE8 and subtracted from note index $63 before the frequency-template update.
Set X=three and tail-call $3B6E to classify display object three's horizontal/depth relation to the player. The main motion loop handles other slots separately.

Patch the source read at $0D3A from X/Y, set its destination high byte to $66, and copy bytes in order into $6665,X starting with X zero. Stop at sentinel $FD without copying it. This initializes wheel flags, selected slots, geometry, dictionary indices, availability/count arrays and related state from an overlay descriptor.
Low byte of the self-modified source address in LDA at $0D3A, set from X by $0D2D. Its high byte is at $0D3C and the copy runs until source byte $FD.

High address byte of the source LDA at $0D3A. The continuation recognizes sentinel $FD, otherwise stores each byte through the separately patched destination $6665,X and advances until the descriptor terminates. It is an operand within $0D2D.
High byte of STA $6665,X in the descriptor copy. $0D2D sets it to $66 before copying; the source's $FD sentinel ends the loop without a store.

Initialize the resident display/IRQ services, set costume bases, and choose/load a save slot. Repeatedly service scene requests and costume rendering, wait for ten IRQ ticks, update object motion, service command wheels and the load-dependent room callback, then advance the random seed. The opening overlay is entered through the same resident load/menu path; its later callbacks retain their overlay-specific meaning.
Wait until the IRQ-maintained counter at $0353 reaches ten, clear it, and return. This paces the main graphical loop; it is not a disk-transfer wait.

1-byte resident field at $0F1D, holding FA in the captured opening. Direct code references: $0F26 lda $0F1D; $0F7E sta $0F1D; $1074 lda $0F1D; $62BE sta $0F1D. These are the direct instruction accesses in the decoded image; indexed access bounds and indirect callers require their enclosing routine. The listed bytes describe the captured value.

Blank the display and, on first initialization, configure the processor port and call the initial $7900 loader. Disable interrupts, select port $25, clear workspace, copy initial hidden-RAM data, initialize sprites and screen, and install NMI/IRQ vectors. Reset sound, select the display bank/memory mode, enable raster IRQs, acknowledge CIA state, and disable the CIA timers through their control bytes. Enable all sprite slots before resuming interrupts and servicing sound. Subsequent entries skip the initial loader/copy according to $0F1D.
Clear zero-page bytes $10-$FF with an increasing Y loop. Processor port, stack and the lower zero-page fields are outside this loop.

Clear pages $0200/$0300, establish initial object order/buffer indices, mark four object/action entries inactive, and set display/message/input sentinels. Seed the keyboard queue with one $FD control, set queue length one, and mark room text modes $0343/$0344 negative. These are generated runtime initial values, not an imported screen image.

Operand byte of STA $02DF at $0FFF. The continuation of $0FB1 initializes keyboard queue length and its initial control byte, disables the scene marker mode, and marks room text-mode fields negative before returning at $1019.

Clear all 1,024 screen bytes at $CC00-$CFFF and all 2,048 bytes at $E000-$E7FF. Fill colour RAM with nine, then choose border/background/shared sprite and character colours. The $E000 range is generated cleared workspace in the opening snapshot, even though later scene resources can load a charset there.

Select port $24 so RAM under I/O/ROM is accessible. On the first initialization only, copy sixteen pages from $8BF8 upward into $E000 upward, incrementing the two self-modified high operands after each page. Restore port $25 and return. Later initializers overwrite portions of that copy, so retained bytes need their producer distinguished from the play-only consumer.

High-address byte of LDA at $107D, incremented for each page of the first-boot sixteen-page copy. The paired destination high operand at $1082 advances in parallel before the routine restores I/O visibility.

High byte of STA $E000,Y at $1080. The page-copy loop increments this byte and the source high byte after each 256-byte page, for sixteen pages, then restores port $25. This label is an operand inside $106E, not a new routine entry.

Clear $FF00-$FF7F, both pages $E800/$E900, and the 64-byte sprite at $FF80-$FFBF. Set that sprite's offsets ten and thirteen to $28. Select mode zero and clear the three allocated sets of seven sprite-strip buffers through $5AE8, reset projected sprite X bytes/high-bit state, and set VIC expansion/priority/collision and multicolour controls. The cleared/constructed sprite bytes are runtime output.

Clear scale input $12 and assign player/fourth-object costume bases $7900, with two other object bases $A000. If slot-menu state $63E6 is nonnegative, reset the selected disk-side cache and request side one through $5698; otherwise retain the loaded side. This sets bases without interpreting costume records.

Save A, X, and Y; select I/O with processor-port value $25; arm the raster chain through $1267; acknowledge VIC and CIA interrupts, update counters, and call frame services before restoring the saved banking and registers. The individual service purposes remain open.
RTI is the complete NMI target held in $FFFA/$FFFB in the opening snapshot.

Copy object render state, depth/colour fields, and display order into the raster service's zero-page slot arrays. Refresh sprite pointer sequences through $4984 when allocation/order changed. Derive horizontal expansion masks and duplicate per-object colours for two- or three-sprite strips according to mode. Negative mode also copies projected positions back to the object coordinates. Copy the fourth-object colour to its pair and clear pending swap counter $63.
Set raster compare to $3D, install $127C in the hardware IRQ vector, clear the border color, and return.

Preserve Y and expose I/O. Load six sprite X positions from $02CC-$02D1, combine their high-X bits with the fourth object's pair, install expansion state and two- or three-sprite costume pointers, and copy colours. Install the fourth object's coordinates, pointers and colours in sprites six and seven. Place the first six sprites at Y=$46, acknowledge raster/CIA IRQ state, schedule line $50 and handler $136F, restore banking/Y, and RTI. The IRQ chain reuses the sprite slots for later vertical strips.

Preserve Y and expose I/O. If the scene view is active, write its fine-scroll and character-memory selection from $62/$030F. Move the first six sprites to Y=$5B, acknowledge IRQ state, schedule raster line $59, and select the next two-/three-sprite-strip handler by mode. Restore the main program's banking and Y before RTI. This handler advances the vertical strip chain rather than the game clock.

Preserve Y and install six sprite pointers at $CFF8-$CFFD from strip-start fields $81/$82/$83, using successive pointers in groups of 2. Continue through the shared tail: select port $25, schedule raster $63 and handler $1430, acknowledge VIC/CIA IRQ state, restore bank $61 and Y, and RTI. This is the 2-sprite-per-object variant for this vertical band; the paired entry selects the other grouping.

Preserve Y and install six sprite pointers at $CFF8-$CFFD from strip-start fields $81/$83, using successive pointers in groups of 3. Continue through the shared tail: select port $25, schedule raster $63 and handler $1430, acknowledge VIC/CIA IRQ state, restore bank $61 and Y, and RTI. This is the 3-sprite-per-object variant for this vertical band; the paired entry selects the other grouping.

Preserve Y, expose I/O, and move sprite slots zero through five to Y=$70. Schedule raster $6D; negative mode $26 selects pointer handler $1479, otherwise $1499. Acknowledge VIC/CIA state, restore the main bank and Y, and RTI. Reusing these hardware slots presents the next vertical strip of the composed costume buffers.

Write character/screen selector $34 and control $1B, schedule line $D9 and handler $17E9, acknowledge IRQ state, and restore bank/Y. The next handler installs the lower object markers.

If $0357 is nonnegative, return without queuing. Otherwise use A as an index into $1FA9: its first byte's complement selects a sound slot and the following byte can select a second slot. Store the request index in $1BB1 for those slots. The periodic sound service consumes these queued indices.

Scan seven pending slots $1BB1 and start queued streams through $1C9F. For each bit enabled in active mask $1C0A, call $1D31 to update that slot, then make a second pass writing its control state through $1F13. Slots zero through two map to SID voices; higher slots are control/filter streams whose hardware writes are gated by their slot number.

Set stream directory pointers $E3/$E4 to $1F33 and $E5/$E6 to $1F6E. For each enabled slot, AND its control byte with zero-page $FE and write the result through $1F13. Mark $0357 negative and clear active mask $1C0A. The actual clear mask comes from $FE rather than an immediate constant.

Move request A into Y and clear the selected pending slot to $FF, then enter $1CA5. The shared entry chooses voice/control mode by slot, reads the stream pointer through the split directory $E3/$E5, and consumes its header. Voice headers include a per-frame callback and filter-routing nibble; slot three supplies filter/resonance and volume state. Advance past that header, set the active-slot bit, and decode the first event through $1D93.

Read filter-routing/resonance from stream ($9F),Y, OR it into cached $1BA4, and write SID $D417. Read the next byte into cached $1BA3 and SID $D418. Y returns advanced once; the caller accounts for both consumed bytes.
Reload slot X from $1C05 and add Y+1 to its low/high stream pointer at $1BB8/$1BBF, carrying into the high byte. The event parser uses this after consuming a variable-length record.

Operand byte of LDX $1C05 at $1D1F. The sound event-pointer helper reloads the slot from that address, increments Y to count consumed bytes, and adds that byte to the stream pointer with carry into its high byte. This symbol does not start a separate instruction.

Set voice/control mode from X and preserve the slot in $1C05. Decrement the slot's two-byte delay; on underflow decode another event at $1D93. Otherwise add its two-byte pitch/filter increment to the cached value. Slots below three can tail-call a nonzero callback pointer stored at $1BAB/$1BAE. When no callback takes over, write the cached value through $1EF2.

Zero the selected slot's two-byte countdown $1BE9/$1BE2 and two-byte increment $1BF7/$1BF0. It leaves the cached value and stream pointer unchanged; event flags use it to cancel an earlier duration or slide.

Read a flag byte from the selected slot's stream pointer. In voice mode its low bit controls gate; bit one ends the active stream and can chain to a new directory entry. Bit two loads a two-byte cached value, and unless bit six is set also reads its duration and increment; otherwise clear the slide. Bit three loads voice envelope bytes with a gate-off write before restoring the event gate. Bit four introduces subflags for direct frequency writes, filter/volume/cutoff fields, and a new delay. Bit five replaces the control byte's high nibble. Bit seven implements counted backward stream loops; other events advance past their consumed bytes. Hardware writes are restricted by the selected slot's voice/control mode. The parser maintains its variable record offset in Y and the active mask in $1C0A.

These pages are loaded scene data consumed by the resident placement routine.

1-byte resident field at $5516, holding 00 in the captured opening. Direct code references: $54EC sta $5516; $54F4 bit $5516; $550C stx $5516; $5512 ldx $5516. These are the direct instruction accesses in the decoded image; indexed access bounds and indirect callers require their enclosing routine. The listed bytes describe the captured value.
Four resource-name selector bytes used by $54F1.

A=$FF clears the view through $5A8D. Otherwise increment the requested scene/title index, place it in $6994, and call the message-window selector $699C. Mark view-change flag $02C4 negative in either case.

Hide four display objects while preserving their active states at $5083, request/wait for the buffer swap, disable drawing through $0310, and invoke $6A0B to present the outgoing view state. Restore the object states, invalidate resource-cache keys with dash, and mark $0533 negative so the outgoing preparation is not repeated on the same request.

Load and unpack the scene map/metadata into $0600, then process its resource selectors. A changed picture selector loads packed data to $BC00 and invalidates costume scale caches; a changed overlay selector loads at $8B00; a changed character selector loads/unpacks at $E000 and clears its final sixteen bytes. A non-dash extra resource selector can load a costume through $56E5. Failed file reads reset the relevant cache to dash and retry from the family entry. Finally derive map masks $5E/$5F/$60, coordinate increments, and mode $26 from the metadata. This resident routine is present in the opening but loads later scene data only when requested.

Remember the requested disk number in A and repeatedly call $19CC until it matches. Show the appropriate insert/turn-disk message through $551B, wait for a keyboard-queue event through $5DE5, and retry. Transition autosaving can require the old side before the new side.

1-byte resident field at $56C4, holding 01 in the captured opening. Direct code references: $5698 sta $56C4; $569E cmp $56C4. These are the direct instruction accesses in the decoded image; indexed access bounds and indirect callers require their enclosing routine. The listed bytes describe the captured value.
Load the two-character file cached at $508F/$5090 into $7900, with a buffer end at $8B00. Retry when the custom loader returns carry set. The opening setup selects AF for female and AV for male.
Load the file cached at $5091/$5092 into $E800 with end page $EB00, retrying on receive error. This buffer is separate from the packed room character data at $E000.
Load the two-character costume filename cached at $5093/$5094 into $A000 with end page $BC00. Retry on carry set. The scene setup chooses the filename through the character-type table at $5969.

Preserve the two-byte random state at $0502/$0503, clear pages $0400 and $0500, restore that state, and install initial progression values and $FF sentinels. Call $4210 once and save its returned state at $0501.

1-byte resident field at $5784, holding 36 in the captured opening. Direct code references: $5728 sta $5784; $5748 lda $5784. These are the direct instruction accesses in the decoded image; indexed access bounds and indirect callers require their enclosing routine. The listed bytes describe the captured value.

1-byte resident field at $5785, holding 25 in the captured opening. Direct code references: $572E sta $5785; $574E lda $5785. These are the direct instruction accesses in the decoded image; indexed access bounds and indirect callers require their enclosing routine. The listed bytes describe the captured value.

Clear side-transfer flag $058C, then enter the shared save preparation at $578B. Copy live inventory and clock to saved fields, clear $04FF, calculate checksum bytes $05FC/$05FD, request the appropriate disk side when one is selected, write the two 256-byte slot sectors through $57A8, and update cached slot name/side through $63E7. A zero side selection skips the sector writes.

Switch wheel display through $620F, clear serialization offset $04FF, prepare mutable game state through $5840, and store random seed $9D/$9E into $05FC/$05FD. Continue with the disk/slot write path at $57A0: a nonzero side selector first calls $5698; save name and sector details come from the current slot.

Write the $0400 and $0500 pages to two track-18 sectors selected by the active save slot at $6297, then update the slot-name state through $63E7. This is persistent game state, not the emulator snapshot format.
Read the active slot's two track-18 sectors into $0400 and $0500 using the sector tables at $5807/$580B, then refresh the change-log index and player-name display through $5871 and $622D.
Four first-sector selectors read by the save/load paths at $57B5/$57E8 with the selected slot index in Y. The matching second-sector table is $580B.
Four second-sector selectors read at $57C4/$57F7 for the slot operation. Each follows its first-sector transfer, giving the two chunks of serialized state.

Iterate 84 mutation entries. For each record belonging to current scene $0531, replace the map cell at its saved index when different. If the saved value already equals the loaded map, clear that redundant record from all three arrays and set $04FF to one. This preserves the distinction between loaded scene data and persistent modifications.

Initialize checksum high byte from $5096. With A as the initial low accumulator, sum byte pairs at $03FF+X and $04FD+X for X=$FE down to one, carrying into $9E after each addition. Store the low checksum at $9D. The caller controls initial A; the routine does not load it with zero itself.
Recalculate the checksum through $5840, compare its low/high bytes with $05FC/$05FD, and on mismatch jump to $5725 to initialize a new state. Equal checksums return with the loaded state intact.

Apply recorded map changes through $585C. Supply a pending scene from the saved active scene if needed, set the active scene sentinel to zero, and derive a default entry from player coordinates when absent. Normalize the default costume filename to AV when its prefix is not A, marking $04FF for correction. Sum the forty name/state bytes at $0504 with carry left by that loop into seed byte $0500. This routine prepares the loaded state before scene loading; it does not read a disk itself.

Mask A to its low nibble and store it in the map cell at $0600,Y, caching value and cell index at $5928/$5929. Early scenes below two and scene four return without recording. Other scenes enter $58DE to preserve the mutation in the save-state arrays.

Search 84 records for the current scene and cached cell index. Reuse a matching record; otherwise take an empty scene slot, or randomly replace one belonging to another scene when full. Store scene at $0400,X, cell at $0455,X, and replacement low-nibble value at $04AA,X. These parallel arrays make persistent map changes part of saved state.

1-byte resident field at $5928, holding 00 in the captured opening. Direct code references: $58CA sta $5928; $5921 lda $5928. These are the direct instruction accesses in the decoded image; indexed access bounds and indirect callers require their enclosing routine. The listed bytes describe the captured value.

1-byte resident field at $5929, holding 00 in the captured opening. Direct code references: $58CD sty $5929; $58ED cmp $5929; $591B lda $5929. These are the direct instruction accesses in the decoded image; indexed access bounds and indirect callers require their enclosing routine. The listed bytes describe the captured value.
Thirty-six ASCII suffix bytes used by $51BF with scene index $0531. A changed suffix triggers $557A to load the corresponding picture resource; paired filename construction supplies its prefix.
Twenty-seven signed scene-to-object-slot selectors. $5194 reads one for scene $0531; negative skips the special availability update, nonnegative clears $037E plus that slot.
Fourteen two-byte ASCII resource names. $5241 doubles costume selector Y, loads the pair and compares it with cached $5093/$5094 before the costume-resource load.

Offset 1 in scene_costume_resource_names ($5969-$5984). Fourteen two-byte ASCII resource names. $5241 doubles costume selector Y, loads the pair and compares it with cached $5093/$5094 before the costume-resource load.
Fourteen initial animation values indexed by the costume selector $071A; $520D copies the selected byte into both object animation state fields $0245/$0246.
Fourteen initial phase/direction values indexed with the same costume selector; $5216 copies them into $0261/$0262.
Seven masks $FF,$7F,$3F,$1F,$0F,$07,$03 used at $565C to keep the lower map bits in the serialized map-change operation.
Seven masks $00,$80,$C0,$E0,$F0,$F8,$FC, complementary to the low-mask entries at $59A1; $5665 combines the selected higher bits in the save/map operation.

Convert a pending discrete-camera cell $02C3 into a scene request when appropriate, supply its default entry, and clear the cell request. A nonnegative requested scene closes the wheels and calls $5098. Update costume rendering for player and other display objects according to mode, derive fourth-object state, and after a scene load request/wait for the sprite swap, rebuild the scene view at $5A34, restore wheels, and clear load/request/action flags. Negative scene requests perform costume updates without a scene load.

1-byte resident field at $5A33, holding 00 in the captured opening. Direct code references: $5A7B sty $5A33; $5A81 ldy $5A33. These are the direct instruction accesses in the decoded image; indexed access bounds and indirect callers require their enclosing routine. The listed bytes describe the captured value.

Write metadata background colours to VIC $D022/$D023 and cache the display colour. Select the message palette or banked colour-table setup according to graphical/grid mode. Hold the camera during redraw through $4261 and call $4C01 for all sixteen scene rows from fifteen down to zero, then release the hold.

Wait for frame-change byte $030D to change, then clear screen cells $CCA0-$CF6F to zero. The upper command-wheel rows before $CCA0 and sprite pointers after this range are left outside this clear loop.

Choose buffer index Y from mode and the object's previous allocation, trying to avoid the other occupied indices in continuous mode. Cache the allocation at $0254,X, then enter $5AE8 to construct seven sprite-strip pointers and clear their working bytes. In continuous mode a companion allocation is stored at $0255,X.

Read low/high buffer bases from $5B33/$5B39 using Y. Put the shared low byte into seven pointers $40-$4D and advance each high byte by three pages. Clear offsets below $C0 or $80 according to mode in all seven buffers. The clear is implemented as a descending loop including offset zero.
Six low bytes $00,$80,$00,$80,$00,$80. Paired with $5B39, these select one of six interleaved half-page costume-buffer bases in $5AE8.
Six high bytes $EA,$EA,$EB,$EB,$EC,$EC paired with $5B33. $5AE8 derives seven strip pointers spaced three pages apart, then clears $80 or $C0 bytes per strip according to mode $26.
Eight colour-band selectors 4,5,6,7,0,1,2,3. $5B85 remaps X when mode Y>=2; $5BAB applies the same remap on the second pass when the saved mode has bit zero set.
Eight first-row offsets 0,4,8,12 repeated. $5BE3 supplies the chosen offset in Y to the first $10-cell colour-RAM fill at $5C2F.
Eight final-row lengths 8,12,16,20 repeated. $5C0E supplies the selected count for the last colour-RAM row fill.

1-byte resident field at $5B57, holding 00 in the captured opening. Direct code references: $5BEE lda $5B57; $5C32 sty $5B57. These are the direct instruction accesses in the decoded image; indexed access bounds and indirect callers require their enclosing routine. The listed bytes describe the captured value.

1-byte resident field at $5B58, holding 00 in the captured opening. Direct code references: $5B7E sta $5B58; $5BCD ldy $5B58; $5BD0 inc $5B58. These are the direct instruction accesses in the decoded image; indexed access bounds and indirect callers require their enclosing routine. The listed bytes describe the captured value.

1-byte resident field at $5B59, holding 00 in the captured opening. Direct code references: $5C2F sta $5B59; $5C48 cpy $5B59. These are the direct instruction accesses in the decoded image; indexed access bounds and indirect callers require their enclosing routine. The listed bytes describe the captured value.

2-byte resident field at $5B5A, holding 00 00 in the captured opening. Direct code references: $5BC7 sta $5B5A; $5C35 ldx $5B5A; $5C4D stx $5B5A. These are the direct instruction accesses in the decoded image; indexed access bounds and indirect callers require their enclosing routine. The listed bytes describe the captured value.

1-byte resident field at $5B5C, holding 00 in the captured opening. Direct code references: $5B76 stx $5B5C; $5B88 sta $5B5C; $5BA5 ldx $5B5C; $5BAE sta $5B5C; $5BCA ldx $5B5C; $5C09 ldx $5B5C. These are the direct instruction accesses in the decoded image; indexed access bounds and indirect callers require their enclosing routine. The listed bytes describe the captured value.

1-byte resident field at $5B5D, holding 00 in the captured opening. Direct code references: $5B79 sty $5B5D; $5BA2 lda $5B5D. These are the direct instruction accesses in the decoded image; indexed access bounds and indirect callers require their enclosing routine. The listed bytes describe the captured value.
Eight offsets $00,$10,...,$70. The per-column loop at $5BD7 adds one to the selected colour-RAM destination base.
Eight low destination bytes $00,$00,$80,$00,$00,$00,$80,$00, paired with $5B6E. $5BD3 adds the column offset and propagates carry into the high byte.
Eight high destination bytes $C0,$C0,$C0,$C1,$C1,$C2,$C2,$C3, paired with $5B66. The fill routine redirects its store through the visible colour-RAM mapping; these are source band coordinates.

Save camera-cell X/Y and set up two passes into RAM lookup destinations beginning near $D89F/$D93F and $D9DF/$DA7F. Select left/right band variant according to the depth cell, then run $5BC5. The stores use patched absolute operands to fill the scene colour-RAM bands in the I/O-visible display path. The dictionary occupies physical RAM at overlapping CPU addresses when I/O is banked out; it is a separate meaning.

Iterate source bands selected through $5B66/$5B6E, adding the band offset $5B5E. Read bounded segments through $99/$9A via $5C2F, step the source by $80 with $5C19, and continue until the output index reaches $A0. $5B47/$5B4F choose the segment starts and lengths; these feed the banked grid colour lookups.

Add $80 to source pointer $99/$9A. On carry into an even high page, subtract two from the high byte, producing the packed/interleaved source traversal used by $5BC5. It does not advance the output index.

A is the exclusive source Y limit, stored at $5B59; Y is the segment start. Starting at output index $5B5A, read bytes through $99/$9A and write both the original byte and its high nibble through two patched absolute STA operands. Increment X/Y until Y reaches the bound and cache the new output index.
Low destination byte of the first patched colour-RAM STA in $5C2F. The setup at $5B76 chooses this band destination before the sampler runs.

High byte of the first colour destination. The continuation shifts the sampled source byte right four places and stores that nibble through the second patched destination before advancing the segment indices.
Low byte of the second patched colour destination in $5C2F, used for the source byte's high nibble.
High byte of the second colour-RAM destination. The continuation increments X/Y, repeats to the requested segment bound, saves output index $5B5A, and returns to the band sampler.
Constant $55 used by the run-length unpacker at $5CF7 for its repeating-pattern token class.
Constant $AA used by the run-length unpacker at $5CFF for its repeating-pattern token class.
Constant $FF used by the run-length unpacker at $5D05 for its repeating-pattern token class.

Read the packed byte count and expanded byte count from a four-byte header. Move the packed block to the end of the configured buffer, then expand it back at its original destination. Tokens $00-$3F copy count+1 literals; $40-$7F repeat the following byte count+1 times; $80-$9F repeat zero; $A0-$BF repeat $55; $C0-$DF repeat $AA; $E0-$FF repeat $FF, using the low five bits plus one for these constant runs. Stop at the declared output end, even within a run. A separate decoder matched the live M2, P2, and C2 expansions byte for byte.

Update the transient-message timer, handle finished-game state through $624B, and call the load-dependent room hook $8C8F. If queued keyboard input exists, dequeue it and dispatch Return, Delete, cursor movement, Space/wheel change, printable input, or the restart control. The hidden-window/early-scene gate restricts which controls are accepted. Finally detect changes in room text mode $0343 and enter $6B63 when that mode changes.

For the final scene, invoke its load-dependent exit hook, then hide display objects, clear the view, request side one, run the slot-menu/load helpers, reset input state, disable interrupts, and jump to $0EF5. The hook meaning depends on the loaded overlay, not on the bytes at that address in another scene's snapshot.

Remember keyboard queue length $02F2, spin until it changes, then decrement it to consume the newly arrived byte without returning its character. Disk-swap and modal callers use this as an acknowledgement.
Store $FF into display-state bytes $71-$74 and return. The following $5E02 is another RTS byte, not a separate hide loop.

Wait until input-enable field $02DF is negative, take the first queued character into X, shift the remaining queue at $02E1 down by one, and decrement $02F2. Y is scratch; the caller dispatches the byte returned in X.

Normalize inventory wheel two to wheel one, clear the previous wheel display, and use the selected verb's object-kind byte $66DC to choose the next wheel and any required companion redraw. Redraw the chosen wheel, clear submit flag $6666 and prefix length $6682, then return. This is the Space/wheel-change behavior rather than a command execution.

X is the signed step. Unless a submit/redraw is pending, retain the old slot, scan in that direction within the wheel's lower/upper bounds, skip unavailable negative flags at $66FB, and accept the new slot or restore the old one at the boundary. Clear the typed prefix and redraw the selected wheel. Changes on the verb wheel can also replace the object/inventory companion wheel according to $66DC.

A nonnegative key enters the prefix matcher at $5F20. A negative submit key clears the active wheel/prefix, selects wheel zero, clears transient-message state, marks submit flag $6666 negative, and prepares any verb-specific companion before reaching the command dispatch at $5F43. The input dispatcher sends Return here; cursor/Delete controls have their own handlers.
Append A through $5F2C, then search the active wheel through $612C. Clear $6666 on return. The caller $5EED supplies a nonnegative key byte; command execution takes its separate negative-byte branch.

A is a typed byte. If prefix length $6682 equals ten, return unchanged. Otherwise store A at $6683 plus that length, subtracting $20 first when A is at least $5B; restore the original A and increment the prefix length. The guard tests equality with ten, not an arbitrary out-of-range length.

Resolve the selected action and right-hand word into dictionary indices $6691/$6692. Scan two-byte action/object pairs at $8B00 through offset $BE, treating zero in either field as a wildcard and a negative first field as an end marker. A match uses its parallel pointer at $8BC0: negative high bytes jump to code, otherwise set high bit and pass the message to $674C. In text mode, call $7903 before the response.
Redraw wheel three through $5FBD and set $6665 to one. This is the special companion layout selected by verbs whose object-kind byte is negative.

Use selected wheel X to obtain its global entry index and screen column/width, move back one entry, advance to the next available entry through $6019, and draw it through $6031. Set $6665 negative after the redraw. This entry draws one companion row rather than the three-row main wheel display.

Derive the selected entry and screen geometry for wheel X. Find the preceding available entry with $5FF6, render it, then twice advance one screen row and available entry with $6019 and render again. $6031 preserves the outer row/entry state around each draw.

Decrement Y until the availability/count byte at $66FB,Y is nonnegative, then return. Wheel sentinel entries and bounds must make that backwards search safe; this helper does not apply a bound of its own.
Read wheel X's width and starting column, then clear width+2 cells in both outer command-wheel rows at $CF70 and $CFC0. Tail-call $61F7 to clear the full typed prefix/highlight.
Add forty to screen index X, increment Y until $66FB,Y is nonnegative, and return the next available entry. This helper relies on the caller's wheel/sentinel configuration for its bound.
Cache wheel X in $665D, add its base $667D,X to selected slot $666D,X, and return the global entry index in Y. A contains the selected slot before the addition.

Y selects an entry in the combined wheel table and X selects a column offset in the $CF70 screen rows. Resolve its dictionary index through $6693, read the word using the hidden-RAM pointer halves $D900/$D800 with port $24 selected, and copy letters through $60AA. Pad to the configured wheel width. Inventory wheel two appends parentheses around entry value plus $31 for values one through nine; zero and values at least ten omit that suffix. The byte for value nine would be a colon, whose player reachability is open.
Low dictionary-word address byte in LDA at $6058, patched from the low pointer table at $D900 before wheel text is emitted.

High-address operand of the self-modified LDA at $6058, not an independent instruction. $6031 reads a dictionary pointer from hidden RAM and patches this byte. The continuation emits the word and padding, restores I/O, and for inventory wheel two optionally writes a parenthesized one-character count using count+$31. The original suffix boundary test covers the resulting digit/colon cases.
Store A in screen row $CF70 at index X and increment X. The caller moves X by forty between the three visible wheel entries.
Clear forty cells in each of the three command-wheel rows at $CF70, $CF98, and $CFC0, then fall through into $60BF to restore their colour/highlight state when visible.

For scene indices at least two, or a nonnegative message-window state, colour the two outer wheel rows six and the middle row three, then restore the active highlight through $61DA. Early scenes with a hidden message window return without those writes. The addresses $DB70/$DB98/$DBC0 mean colour RAM in this I/O-visible path.

In negative mode, hide only when a nonzero scene request is pending. In continuous mode, consider scene five, window request $6994 and visibility $6995 before hiding. A hide clears all three rows' colour RAM, resets prefix and active wheel, and marks the wheel submit/redraw state negative; it does not erase the stored word strings.

Match the uppercase prefix at $6683, length $6682, against available entries of the active wheel. A first letter starts at base plus one with $6679 candidates; a longer prefix starts at the selected slot with $6679 minus that slot candidates. Negative $66FB flags skip an entry. Fold word bytes at least $5B by subtracting $20. On success select the matching slot, highlight the new prefix position, and redraw through $5EB0. On failure write red ($02) to the border and decrement the prefix length, preserving the preceding accepted prefix and selection.
Low dictionary-word address byte in LDA at $6186, patched from $D900 before the bounded wheel-prefix search compares its candidate word.

High-address operand of the self-modified LDA at $6186, patched from the selected dictionary pointer. The continuation case-folds letters, compares the accepted prefix, and on success stores the matching wheel slot and redraws it. Failed candidates advance until the bounded search ends; total rejection restores I/O, sets a red border and discards the last prefix byte. This operand is inside the already tested $612C matcher.

Load accepted prefix length, add the wheel's screen-column base with the incoming carry, and store colour one at $DB97 plus that index. The caller establishes carry as part of its search/selection path.

1-byte resident field at $61D9, holding 00 in the captured opening. Direct code references: $61E2 sty $61D9; $61F0 ldy $61D9. These are the direct instruction accesses in the decoded image; indexed access bounds and indirect callers require their enclosing routine. The listed bytes describe the captured value.

For each accepted prefix character from the saved length down to one, add its wheel screen-column base and store colour one in the middle row at $DB98. Zero prefix length returns unchanged. $61D9 temporarily holds the loop length across index computation.

Restore fourteen colour cells beginning at $DB98 plus the active wheel's column offset to colour three, then set prefix length $6682 to zero. The selected word at $666D plus wheel number is preserved; the previously stored prefix bytes are left in the buffer.

Copy inventory entries one through twenty-three from $6729 into persistent fields $054C, skipping entry zero. Copy second/minute/hour fields $0374-$0376 into $0571-$0573. The disk save helper calls this before serializing the state.

Copy saved inventory entries one through twenty-three from $054C back into $6729, and restore seconds/minutes/hours from $0571-$0573. Entry zero is intentionally outside the descending nonzero-Y loop.

A negative $0580 means continue play. Otherwise disable sprite display; state zero presents message request $21, and states other than two run the end-overlay setup at $6450 then its $7900 entry. Present message $1F, wait for a keyboard acknowledgement, stop sound, and restart through $5DB6. This is an end-state dispatcher, not joystick polling.
When $62DD is nonnegative, load the DS slot-menu overlay and run it at $BC00; otherwise load the retained selected slot through $57D1. Clear the load/menu flags $62DD/$63E6 on completion.

1-byte resident field at $6297, holding 00 in the captured opening. Direct code references: $57B2 ldy $6297; $57C1 ldy $6297; $57E5 ldy $6297; $57F4 ldy $6297; $62B3 sty $6297; $62F8 sty $6297; $6301 sta $6297; $6321 ldy $6297; $6353 ldy $6297; $638E ldy $6297; $63E7 lda $6297; $6403 ldx $6297; $648C lda $6297; $64B1 ldx $6297; $6520 sty $6297; $BC0C sty $6297; $BC21 sta $6297; $BC2C sta $6297; $BC37 sta $6297; $BC9F sty $6297. These are the direct instruction accesses in the decoded image; indexed access bounds and indirect callers require their enclosing routine. The listed bytes describe the captured value.

1-byte resident field at $6298, holding 00 in the captured opening. Direct code references: $62FE lda $6298; $6317 ldy $6298; $648F sta $6298. These are the direct instruction accesses in the decoded image; indexed access bounds and indirect callers require their enclosing routine. The listed bytes describe the captured value.

Replace the dialog action word at $65BB-$65BE with load, initialize the slot dialog, and get a selected slot. Store it, derive the retained disk-side state through $63D1, mark a loaded-game restart, invalidate resource caches, enable interrupts, and restart the resident main entry at $0EF5.

Put dash ($2D) in map/picture/charset/overlay/extra-resource cache keys $5088/$508A/$508C/$508E/$5092/$5094. Subsequent resource loading treats the cached files as absent and reloads needed selectors.

1-byte resident field at $62DD, holding 00 in the captured opening. Direct code references: $627D lda $62DD; $6290 sta $62DD; $62BB sta $62DD; $6530 sta $62DD; $BCAF sta $62DD. These are the direct instruction accesses in the decoded image; indexed access bounds and indirect callers require their enclosing routine. The listed bytes describe the captured value.

Replace the slot dialog's action word with save, open the dialog and read its selected slot. Run the side-aware save procedure at $6307, restore the earlier slot selection from $6298, and close the dialog through $6537.

Preserve the active scene as the pending scene, switch to scene-one save context and mark $058C. Compare old/new slot side states in $642B to decide whether to save one or both disk sides. The two-side paths temporarily mark $054C negative so the alternate side keeps its required state; $638E can avoid overwriting a differently named slot without the needed side transition. Restore the active scene from the pending value afterward.

Choose one of three ten-byte cached names at $640D/$6417/$6421 by selected slot. Compare the current saved player name at $0504 until zero or ten characters. Return carry set at the first mismatch and clear on equal/terminated name; the save-side decision consumes that carry.
Byte 1 of the instruction at $63C4 (cmp $640D,x). This is a patched operand/instruction alias, not a separately callable routine. Execution continues on the enclosing instruction boundaries.
Byte 2 of the instruction at $63C4 (cmp $640D,x). This is a patched operand/instruction alias, not a separately callable routine. Execution continues on the enclosing instruction boundaries.
Read selected slot state $642B,Y and return Y=$FF for state two or Y=zero otherwise. Cache the player costume filename suffix $052F into $5090 before returning to the load-game restart caller.
One zero byte between the RTS at $63E5 and the save-name routine at $63E7. No instruction falls through the preceding RTS; this is a bounded separator, not a BRK continuation of the slot helper.

Compute ten times selected slot index $6297 and copy ten bytes of the saved player name at $0504 into its entry in $640D-$642A. Store current disk-side value $5095 in slot state $642B,X. The menu later uses these cached names/states before selecting a save.
First twenty bytes of the three ten-character save-slot name buffers; $63E7 copies the current player name into the selected ten-byte row.
Third ten-character save-slot name buffer; DS setup writes it at $BD08, and $657A displays it through the patched slot-name copier.
Three per-slot disk/side selector bytes; $6409 records the selected disk value and $63D1 reads it when choosing a slot.

1-byte resident field at $642E, holding 00 in the captured opening. Direct code references: $63EB sta $642E; $63F1 adc $642E. These are the direct instruction accesses in the decoded image; indexed access bounds and indirect callers require their enclosing routine. The listed bytes describe the captured value.
Repeatedly request file DS into $BC00-$CBFF until the disk reader returns carry clear, then hide display objects. The loaded code begins at $BC00 and contains the three-slot selection UI.

Set filename letters L/R and the disk-reader destination/limit fields for the $7900 end overlay, retry the shared file reader on carry-set failure, then return. The caller enters that overlay at $7900 after the load.

Hide sprites, clear the keyboard queue and wait for pending display updates. Disable normal scene drawing, clear view/message areas and preserve the selected slot. Inventory slot 23, at $6729+$17, whose dictionary entry is ticket. A negative byte marks it unavailable; zero represents one ticket. $90F4 tests its sign at the counter, and the purchase path stores zero after charging the dollar entry. Other nonnegative values also pass this sign test.

Clear the upper message area, set the message timeout to twenty, point output at $CC00, and render the two-byte-header stream through $6782. If text colour is at least five, write the corresponding colour-RAM byte and a rounded marker glyph near the indent. Mark the transient message displayed through $6749/$674A.

Read the stream's first byte as a layout parameter and its second as an optional nonzero colour. Let $6942 adjust the indent for a graphical speaker, clamp the header's low-five-bit indent to the available indent, and initialize the output column and marker position. Enter the shared parser at $67B7 with Y=1 so text starts after the two-byte header.

Operand of STX $6997 at $67AD in the headered-message entry. After initializing the column, the routine increments Y from zero to one and calls $67B7, whose first increment starts text at offset two, then returns to its caller.

Begin with Y=$FF so the shared parser at $67B7 advances to the stream's first byte. Zero flushes and ends; $FF flushes a line. $FB-$FE select dictionary-word substitutions, while $F6-$FA alter cursor or formatting state. The literal marker $40 is suppressed; other bytes pass to $6891.

Increment Y and read the stream at $10/$11. Zero finishes the line and returns; $FF finishes a line and continues. $FB-$FE choose dictionary insertion with capitalization and/or a following space through $68D4. Controls $FA/$F9/$F8 emit opening glyphs one/five/two and select closing glyphs three/six/four; $F7 finishes one or two lines according to colour, emits glyph seven and chooses closing glyph eight. $F6 invokes the rewind helper, $40 is skipped, and other bytes go to $6891. This is the same parser as the $67B5 entry, with the caller supplying an existing Y offset.

Emit the deferred closing glyph $691F if nonzero, clear it, advance/scroll the output through $6A4E, and reset the output column $6997 to indent $0342. The test harness can intercept this whole drawing operation while checking text-token output.

Subtract forty from low output-pointer byte $99. The code computes a borrow into a loaded $9A but does not store that high result, so the high pointer byte remains unchanged even when the low byte wraps. If message-window state $6995 is nonnegative, decrement its row counter $6996. The effect is a low-byte rewind, not an unrestricted sixteen-bit pointer subtraction.

Preserve parser index Y in $691E, store glyph A at output pointer $99/$9A plus column $6997, and save that pointer. Add $0C00 to address the matching colour cell, temporarily expose I/O with port $25, and write text colour $0341. Restore the prior banking and output pointer, increment the column, and restore Y. The glyph renderer reads the physical RAM font separately through the VIC.

Read the word index after a $FB-$FE token. Bank I/O out with port $24; use the high-byte table $D800 and low-byte table $D900 to patch the source of an indexed LDA. Emit bytes until zero. A negative $6920 subtracts $20 from the first character; bit zero appends a space. Restore port $25 and resume the parent stream.
Low address byte of the self-modified dictionary LDA at $68EB, paired with $68ED. The parser patches it from $D900 for the selected dictionary index.

High-address operand of the dictionary LDA at $68EB, patched from the split pointer table by $68D4. After each byte, the continuation applies first-letter subtraction only once, writes glyphs through $6891, and retains only the optional-space bit. At the word terminator it can append a space, restores port $25, and returns to the stream parser at $67B7.

Set fine-scroll byte $62 to $17, copy default message colour into four palette bands, and fill fifteen rows from $CCA0 through $CEF7 with spaces. Clear the following three rows to zero, reset row/column counters, and set output pointer to $CCA0. Colour initialization is delegated to $6AEF.

Fill colour RAM in five segments spanning $D8A0-$DB1F, using palette bytes $6998-$699B. Two middle segments share $6999. In the normal display path these stores reach colour RAM; the hidden-RAM dictionary overlaps the CPU addresses only under different banking.

Copy fourteen rows upward by forty cells in three bounded chunks beginning at $CCC8, $CD90 and $CE58, ending with the source row at $CED0. Then fill thirty-eight cells beginning at $CED0 with spaces. The final row's two remaining cells are outside the clear loop, which begins with X=$25.

Set room text mode $0343 and reset window, wheel, display and selected action state. Select one of three run-length streams through pointer pairs at the load-dependent $8C80 table. Each nonzero count byte is followed by a glyph byte repeated that many times into the $CCA0-based screen; output-page and input-page bytes advance on wrap. Count zero ends the stream and jumps to the corresponding load-dependent hook at $8C86/$8C89/$8C8C. These addresses hold different meanings in different overlays; the opening's location-state bytes are not those graphical streams.

High operand byte of STA $CCA0,X at $6BD5, initialized to $CC and incremented on output-index wrap. The continuation repeats the current glyph count, fetches the next count/value pair, and on zero count dispatches one of the three room text hooks according to $0343.

32 high bytes paired with $6C3F for positive scene/title message requests. Some scene indices intentionally share a title pointer. The next high-byte table at $6C22 serves high-bit object-description requests.

29 high bytes paired with $6C5F for object/terminal descriptions. $699C clears the request high bit before indexing this view. The final slot is a mutable custom-dialog pointer, patched by menu and interaction routines.
